title: Java Slide 3
description: Practice test covering Java classes, instance variables, access modifiers, constructors, primitive vs. reference types, floating-point numbers, Scanner input, and formatted output.

questions.prompt: What is the exact output printed when the following Java program is compiled and executed?

options.text: empty 0.0 false
null 0 false
null 0.0 false
null 0.0 true
null 0.00 false

questions.explanation: Reference-type instance variables like String default to null, numeric primitive instance variables like double default to 0.0, and boolean instance variables default to false. The format specifier %.1f outputs 0.0 with one digit after the decimal point.

questions.prompt: What is the exact result of attempting to compile and run the following code?

options.text: Compile-time error: local variable initialDeposit might not have been initialized
It compiles and prints 0.00 because double variables always default to 0.0
It compiles and prints 50.00 because initialDeposit is assigned in the if block
It compiles and prints 10.00 because bonus is the only initialized variable
Runtime exception: NullPointerException when printf reads initialDeposit

questions.explanation: Unlike instance variables, local variables are not automatically initialized by default. The Java compiler issues a compilation error whenever code attempts to read a local variable that is not guaranteed to be initialized before use.

questions.prompt: What is the exact output printed by the following code snippet?

options.text: [Jane Green][John Blue]
[Jane][Green]
[Jane][John Blue]
[Jane Green][ ]
[Jane][ Green]

questions.explanation: Scanner method next() reads characters only until the first whitespace character is encountered, returning "Jane" and leaving " Green" on the first line. The subsequent call to nextLine() reads the remaining characters on that line up to the newline character, returning " Green" including the leading space.

questions.prompt: What happens when you attempt to compile and execute the following Java class?

options.text: It compiles and prints "5 Items" to the standard output
Compile-time error: primitive variable count cannot be used to invoke a method
Compile-time error: main cannot access private instance variables of TypeTest
It compiles and prints "0 null" because instance variables reset in main
Runtime exception: NullPointerException when invoking toString() on count

questions.explanation: The instance variable count is of primitive type int, which stores a single value rather than a reference to an object. A primitive-type variable cannot be used to invoke methods, causing a compile-time error on test.count.toString().

questions.prompt: What is the exact result of attempting to compile and run the following code?

options.text: It compiles and prints "50.00 0.00" using the compiler's default constructor
It compiles and prints "50.00 50.00" by copying the previous object's state
Runtime exception: NullPointerException when calling a2.getBalance()
Compile-time error: no suitable no-argument constructor found for Account()
Compile-time error: class Account must be declared public in its own file

questions.explanation: When a class declares a custom constructor, the Java compiler does not create a default no-argument constructor for that class. Consequently, calling new Account() with no arguments causes a compilation error.

questions.prompt: What is the exact output printed when the following program is executed?

options.text: Default: $35.50
Default: $15.50
Jane: $5.50

questions.explanation: In the constructor, name = name assigns the local parameter to itself rather than updating this.name, leaving the instance variable name as "Default". The negative initial balance (-20.0) and negative deposit (-10.0) are ignored by the > 0.0 checks, so only 35.5 is added and formatted by %.2f as 35.50.

questions.prompt: What is the exact output produced when the following program is run?
questions.explanation: Reference variables a1 and a2 refer to the same Account object in memory, so a2.deposit(cash) updates that object's balance to 25.256. Because method parameters are local variables, setting amount = 0.0 does not affect cash in main, and %.2f rounds both values to two decimal places as 25.26 and 15.26.

questions.prompt: What is the exact result of compiling and running the following Java program?

options.text: null 25.5
null 15.5
Compile-time error: no no-argument constructor found for class Account
Compile-time error: method Account cannot have the same name as its class
empty 25.5

questions.explanation: Constructors cannot specify return types, so public void Account(String, double) is a regular method rather than a constructor, and the compiler still provides a default no-argument constructor that initializes name to null and balance to 0.0. Calling deposit(10) invokes deposit(int) (adding 20) and deposit(5.5) invokes deposit(double) (adding 5.5), yielding null 25.5.

questions.prompt: What is the exact result when the following program is compiled and executed?

options.text: It compiles and prints "60.00" after transferring 40.0 to primary
It compiles and prints "100.00" because transferTo ignores a null target
Runtime error: NullPointerException when accessing target.balance in transferTo
Compile-time error: transferTo cannot access private field target.balance
Compile-time error: instance variable primary is not initialized before use

questions.explanation: The reference-type instance variable primary is not explicitly initialized, so it receives the default value null. When transferTo attempts to evaluate target.balance on that null reference after subtracting amount from backup.balance, a NullPointerException is thrown at runtime.

questions.prompt: What is the exact output printed when the following program is compiled and executed?
questions.explanation: Arguments are evaluated left-to-right: acc.applyBonus(50) calls applyBonus(int) where integer division 50 / 100 evaluates to 0, leaving balance at 200.0. Next, acc.applyBonus(10.0) calls applyBonus(double) where 10.0 / 100 is 0.10, updating balance to 220.0 before the third argument acc.balance is evaluated.
